title: Applied ML Eval Assets: Prompt Set Catalog, Onboarding & Regression Playbook
author: Priya Shah
summary: This document is the canonical catalog and playbook for applied-ML evaluation assets used by Redwood Inference product, evaluation, and SRE teams. It standardizes prompt-set naming, onboarding steps for new prompt sets and models, quality guardrails, quantization profile linkage, and the regression triage flow.
body:
Overview:
This page consolidates guidance for the eval-harness, prompt sets, benchmarks, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage playbooks. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML researchers, and platform owners running production inference and continuous quality checks.

Goals and scope:
- Provide a single reference for creating, reviewing, and operating prompt sets and benchmark suites used by the eval harness.
- Define onboarding and review steps for new models and prompt sets, including ownership, storage, and required metadata.
- Enumerate quality guardrails (metrics and thresholds) used for automated alerts and human review.
- Link quantization profiles to evaluation workflows and list minimum checks before quantized rollout.
- Describe the regression triage playbook for escalations, prioritization, and rollback.

1) Naming, storage and metadata standards for prompt sets and benchmarks
- Location: All official prompt sets live in S3 at s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/ with a directory per product or vertical: e.g., s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/assistant/faq-resolution/
- File format: JSONL (one JSON object per line). Each object must include: id, prompt, expected_responses (list), tags (list), difficulty, source (internal|synthetic|customer-provided), and created_by.
- Recommended fields (enforced by CI on PRs):
  - id: short uuid-like string (e.g., ps-2029-09-001)
  - prompt: string (no template interpolation at storage time)
  - expected_responses: list of canonical responses or golden outputs for exact/partial matching
  - metrics_to_compute: list (e.g., exact_match, rouge_l, bertscore, helpfulness_rating)
  - tags: [smoke, regression, benchmark, privacy_sensitive]
  - owner: team name and pager (pager channel)
- Versioning: Prompt sets must use semantic file versioning. PRs that modify content must include a changelog entry and a rationale.

2) Onboarding a new prompt set or benchmark suite (step-by-step)
1. Create a proposal PR in the prompt-sets repo with: description, intended use, associated models, and sample stats (size, token distribution).
2. Add metadata file prompt-set-name.metadata.json with fields: owner, contact, expected_metrics, recommended_eval_frequency (daily/weekly/on-commit).
3. Run local eval-harness against the current baseline model and attach result artifacts (CSV or JSON).
4. Reviewer checklist: completeness, data sensitivity, dataset bias check, coverage across edge-cases. At least one reviewer from applied-ml team and one from product/solutions.
5. After approval, CI will copy to s3 and register a record in the eval-catalog (internal index).
6. Notify downstream systems by opening an issue in the eval-tracking board linking the catalog id.

3) Model onboarding checklist (lightweight, production-ready)
- Required artifacts before serving a model on Redwood:
  - Model card (model-card.md) containing architecture, training data summary, license, and failure modes.
  - Eval manifest linking prompt sets and benchmark runs (with commit SHAs).
  - Baseline eval report with metrics and latency cost profile.
  - Quantization profile candidate (if applicable) and recommended routing fallback (non-quantized variant).
  - Security review: PII check, data residency constraints.
- Owners and lanes:
  - Applied ML: responsible for producing the eval manifest and metrics.
  - Eng-serving-runtime: responsible for perf profile, latency SLOs, and kernel compatibility.
  - Product: defines acceptance criteria for business metrics.

4) Quality guardrails and metric thresholds
- Core metrics tracked by the eval pipeline: exact_match, rouge_l, bertscore, response_length_median, hallucination_rate (estimated), latency_p95, token_cost_per_call.
- Example guardrails for release gating:
  - Regression gate: No model may ship if any core metric declines > 2% absolute compared to the gated baseline on the full benchmark suite.
  - Critical regression: If hallucination_rate increases by > 0.5 percentage points on privacy-sensitive prompts, block rollout and trigger incident.
  - Latency SLO: p95 inference latency must be <= target_latency_ms for the planned deployment tier (see product route config).
  - Cost guardrail: Token_cost_per_call must not exceed baseline_cost * 1.2 unless approved by finance.
- Escalation policy: Automated alerts to slack channel #applied-ml-evals for threshold violations; on-call applied-ml responder must triage within 4 hours.

5) Quantization profiles: integration with evals and rollout criteria
- Each quantization profile (e.g., int8-lora-compat, q4f32, q2/ffn) must be stored in docs at /quantization-profiles/ with: name, calibrated_on_model_sha, expected_accuracy_delta_by_metric, recommended_batching, kernel_notes, and owner.
- Minimum quantized rollout checks:
  - Run full prompt-set suite and compare against float baseline. Report accuracy deltas per metric and per tag (smoke/regression/benchmark).
  - Run long-tail prompts (top 5% token length) to validate KV cache behavior.
  - Run integrated latency/cost profile on dedicated infra (matching deployment config).
  - Fail rollout if any metric delta exceeds pre-approved tolerances (see product acceptance table).

6) Regression triage playbook (operational steps)
- Triggering events: automated eval job failing gate, customer-reported regression with repro prompt set, or sudden drift in production metrics.
- Immediate actions (within 1 hour):
  1. Triage owner assigns: on-call applied-ml engineer and runtime engineer.
  2. Capture failing sample set and reproduce locally against the previous good model SHA and current model SHA.
  3. If repro is confirmed on baseline infra, escalate to Incident Response (see oncall-and-incident-response/process).
- Prioritization matrix:
  - P0: customer-facing data corruption, privacy leak, or model hallucination that exposes PII - immediate rollback.
  - P1: broad regression affecting >20% of smoke prompts or >10% of production traffic - patch or rollback within 24 hours.
  - P2: isolated degradation - fix in next sprint with monitoring.
- Recovery steps:
  - Rollback to last known-good model: Coordinate with eng-platform for deployment and with SRE for capacity adjustments.
  - Create a regression report: include root-cause hypothesis, repro prompt set, diff of tokenization/outputs, and mitigation plan.
  - Postmortem: if severity >= P1, schedule postmortem within 72 hours.

7) Continuous evaluation cadence and automation
- Recommended job cadence:
  - On-commit (model or prompt-set change): run smoke suite (fast) and integration tests.
  - Nightly: run full benchmark suite against active candidate and baseline.
  - Weekly: run long-tail and cost analysis jobs (including mixed-batch scenarios).
- CI requirements: Any PR that updates prompt sets or quantization profiles must attach eval artifacts. PRs that change thresholds must be approved by product and applied-ml reviewers.

8) Example prompt-set sample (illustrative JSONL entry)
{"id": "ps-2029-09-001", "prompt": "Summarize the following customer email and extract the main action items:\n[EMAIL] I need the report by Wednesday and please loop in finance.", "expected_responses": ["Summarize: Request for report due Wednesday; Action items: prepare report, notify finance"], "tags": ["summarization","smoke"], "metrics_to_compute": ["exact_match","rouge_l"], "owner": "applied-ml"}

9) Responsibilities and owners
- Applied ML: prompt-set curation, bias and sensitivity reviews, regression triage lead.
- Eng-serving-runtime: latency/throughput profiling, kernel/quantization verification.
- Eng-platform: CI/CD for eval automation, catalog registration, and access controls.
- Product: acceptance criteria for new benchmarks and packaged releases.

10) Appendix: quick links and templates
- Prompt-set metadata template: s3://redwood-evals/templates/prompt-set-metadata.example.json
- Eval harness runbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025.json
- Quantization profiles index: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026.json

Contact and questions:
For questions about adoption or to request a review, ping #applied-ml-evals on Slack or email applied-ml@redwood.ai.
